cross_locale_answer: REUSE OF owner_added_agent: right in all seven, because what transfers is the possessor phrase and each locale rebuilt the verb frame. en drops "own" in both lines ("their agent"), fr/es do the same ("son agent"/"su agente"), while zh ("自己的"), ru ("собственного"), ur ("اپنے"), hi ("अपने") and vi ("của mình") keep the emphatic own-word their sibling uses, so the pairs read in parallel inside each locale. hi/ur had to inflect the possessive to the oblique (अपना->अपने, اپنا->اپنے) for the کو postposition, and did. No locale copied a frame that does not fit "approved ... joining".

placeholders.actor: Display name of the person or agent who made the change; never inflected

sidecar.note: "their" refers to the actor's own agent. The target label already carries the owner in parentheses; that is server data and must never be moved into the sentence. {targets} is a list joined by Intl.ListFormat(conjunction), always exactly one name for this key.

addendum.why: Two corrections/confirmations recorded AFTER this audit's receipts were sealed in i18n/receipts/: (1) the rendered-width measurement I owed under my own overflow rule and had not taken before writing them; (2) my independent reproduction of auditor B's CO-B1 cardinality case. The receipts themselves are immutable and are not rewritten; the rows carry this content through auditor B's receipts (CO-B4 nit, CO-B1 major).

width.method: intl-messageformat at one target with the shipped fixture labels (actor "Sana Ketabchi", target "Aida (Sana Ketabchi)"), measured in terminal cells (East Asian W/F = 2, combining marks = 0); compared with the same render in every other ui.teamBridge.events.* key of that locale and with English.
width.finding: CONFIRMS auditor B's CO-B4. Every locale's line is the longest in the ui.teamBridge.events namespace; fr +20 cells (+32%), ru +17 (+27%), vi +15 (+24%) over English are material. Mechanism, read from team-bridge-member-events.tsx: the sentence sits in a `min-w-0 truncate` span and is wrapped in a Tooltip ONLY when `truncated` (more than TEAM_BRIDGE_EVENT_NAMES_SHOWN = 2 names), so at this key's one-target cardinality an ellipsised line has no affordance that reveals the tail. No copy change proposed here: each phrasing is the locale's correct one and the fix that removes the risk is the cardinality guard plus a rendered check at the timeline column's narrowest supported width.
width.would_record_as: NIT per locale (fr, es, zh-CN, ru, vi, ur, hi), not a major: no rendered evidence of clipping exists and the line wraps/ellipsises inside a scrolling timeline column.

cardinality_case.note: Intl.ListFormat(conjunction) joins two names as this app joins them (team-bridge-member-events.tsx joinNames); the value then renders the singular possessive/noun over a two-name list. This is a SOURCE-side defect of the en sentence (it renders "their agent A and B"), reproduced identically by every locale because each translated the source faithfully. Neither the en test file nor the fixtures contain a multi-target consent event: node --test scripts/team-bridge-member-events.test.mjs passes 23/23 at this head, and its consent case is one target.

ledger_consequence.observed: ledger-assemble.mjs has no way to retire a recorded non-passing audit, and a row only restarts when its source or target bytes change (the stale reset). Auditor B recorded CO-B1 as MAJOR on es, fr, hi, ru and ur, so those five rows read status "changes_requested" and ledger-check fails on them.
ledger_consequence.therefore: A code-only remediation (the agreed one-line guard in teamBridgeEventOwnerConsent) leaves the locale files byte-identical, so the five rows would stay red with no in-tool path to clear them. If the disposition is that CO-B1 is a source-side defect rather than a defect of these translations, the rows need either a locale byte change that legitimately resets them or a manager decision recorded on the PR; this is reported, not decided, by auditor A.
